quickSummary: The frog's carnivorous alimentary canal is short. Teeth are present on the upper jaw (maxillary) and palate roof (vomerine)—homodont, acrodont, and polyphyodont (lower jaw is toothless); teeth hold prey without chewing. The fleshy bifid tongue is attached ANTERIORLY and flips outward. Oxyntopeptic cells secrete HCl and pepsinogen. Bile and pancreatic juice enter the duodenum via a common hepatopancreatic duct. Nutrient absorption occurs across ileum villi.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Teeth are homodont, acrodont, polyphyodont on upper jaw and roof only (lower jaw is toothless). Tongue is attached anteriorly and flips outward.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FROG ALIMENTARY CANAL
                                     │
  Mouth ──► Buccopharyngeal Cavity ──► Oesophagus ──► Stomach (Cardiac/Pyloric)
                                                           │
  Cloaca ◄── Rectum ◄── Ileum ◄── Duodenum ◄───────────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
Frog is a strict carnivore; consequently, its alimentary canal is characteristically short in length relative to its body dimensions.

### Dentition Features
• **Upper Jaw & Roof Only**: Maxillary teeth line the upper jaw; two transverse patches of Vomerine teeth sit on the vomer bones of the palate. The **lower jaw is completely toothless (edentulous)**.
• **Tooth Characteristics**: **Homodont** (all teeth identical), **Acrodont** (attached to bone summit without sockets), **Polyphyodont** (replaced throughout life).
• **Function**: Teeth are **NOT used for chewing**; they strictly hold struggling live prey to prevent escape.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Tongue Mechanics & Prey Capture
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Tongue Mechanics & Prey Capture
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TONGUE PROTRUSION MECHANISM
                          
   Resting State: Tongue folded backward into buccal cavity (Tip facing throat)
                                       │
   Prey Sighted ──► Sublingual lymph sac inflates + Glossal muscles contract
                                       │
   Action: Tongue flips OUTWARD over anterior attachment (Tip strikes prey)
conceptBreakdown.content: The tongue is large, muscular, sticky, vascular, and **bilobed/bifid at the tip**. Crucially, it is **attached at the anterior margin** of the lower jaw and free posteriorly. When prey is sighted, sublingual lymph sacs inflate and glossal muscles contract, causing the tongue to flip rapidly outward over the anterior hinge to strike and entrap insects.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Histophysiology of Digestion & Absorption
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Histophysiology of Digestion & Absorption
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Stomach Digestion**: Food passes through the short esophagus into the stomach:
   - **Oxyntopeptic Cells**: Glandular cells in the gastric mucosa that secrete both Hydrochloric Acid ($\text{HCl}$) and inactive Pepsinogen. $\text{HCl}$ kills prey and activates Pepsin, which digests proteins into peptones.
   - **Chyme**: Acidic semi-liquid pulp passes through the pyloric sphincter into the duodenum.
2. **Digestive Glands & Hepatopancreatic Duct**:
   - **Liver**: Largest trilobed gland; secretes Bile (devoid of enzymes, stored in Gall Bladder) to emulsify fats and neutralize acidity.
   - **Pancreas**: Diffuse gland secreting Pancreatic Juice (trypsinogen, amylase/amylopsin, lipase/steapsin).
   - **Hepatopancreatic Duct**: Common duct delivering bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum.
3. **Absorption**: Digestion finishes in the **Ileum**, whose internal mucosa is folded into absorptive **Villi**. Undigested waste enters the **Rectum** and is expelled through the **Cloaca**.
